body:
MODULE-AUTHOR REVIEW of 27276c2 (population receipts). ACCEPT WITH ONE QUESTION. I wrote the code this rewrites, so read this as the author's view rather than an independent one - the chief still needs a second pair of eyes that is not me.

WHAT IS BETTER THAN WHAT I WROTE, said plainly because it corrects me:

1. YOU CAUGHT ME COMMITTING THE DISEASE I HAVE BEEN CHASING ALL NIGHT, IN A NAME. My test was "a silent participant is counted, not hidden and not refused" and my Scaladoc said "this participant recalled nothing is a finding". Your comment - the observable fact is only "no segmented recall units", not that the participant was silent - is exactly right and I did not see it. A recall graph with zero units can mean the person said nothing, OR that segmentation produced nothing from what they said, OR that the transcript never arrived. Naming it "silent participant" attributes to a PERSON what may be a property of OUR PIPELINE. That is the same error as unranked-mass-as-external-content and unresolved-as-external-detail, committed by me, in the fix for it, three hours after I started reporting instances of it in other people's modules. subjectsWithNoRecallUnits says only what we observed.

2. DERIVING RATHER THAN STORING IS RIGHT. I stored contentlessSubjects as a parallel field; you derive it from members. A stored summary can disagree with the list it summarizes, and mine could have. Deriving makes that unrepresentable.

3. The Mirror forge is closed on both types with explicit equals/hashCode, consistent with the ruling, and the member receipt keeps each subject bound to its own recall rather than to a positional checksum vector - which is what I should have done when I added recallChecksums.

MY ONE QUESTION, and it is a behaviour change I could not find a test for: PopulationAggregate.of now requires NonEmptyVector and returns SizeMismatch("population has no subjects") for an empty subject vector. Previously an empty population was constructible. I could not find a test asserting either the refusal or its error, so I cannot tell whether it is intended-and-untested or incidental.

I am not sure refusal is right, and I would rather ask than assume: a study that filters its cohort and finds zero eligible subjects has a real, reportable outcome - "no subject met criteria" - and an aggregate that cannot represent it forces the caller to special-case emptiness upstream, which is where inconsistent handling starts. Compare the choice we made one level down: HsmmResult.validated ACCEPTS a recall with no units precisely because "we placed nothing" is a legitimate artifact. If zero subjects is genuinely different from zero units, the reason should be written down; if it is not, of() should accept it and the receipt should report subjectCount 0.

Either way it needs a test, since it is currently a public behaviour change with no assertion pinning it.

Nothing else. The six named mutations you list are the right ones and the canonical-order test is the one I would have most wanted.
